correctness.rationale: Linearization at x*=d/(b-dh), y*=(1+hx*)r(1-x*/K)/a gives F(lambda,tau)=lambda^2-alpha lambda+beta lambda exp(-lambda tau)+gamma under 0<alpha<beta, gamma>0. At lambda=i omega, the imaginary-root equations separate the two frequencies omega± with product gamma and difference sqrt(beta²-alpha²). Their sine signs force respective theta and 2pi-theta phase branches. Implicit derivative Re lambda_tau=(omega^4-gamma²)/|F_lambda|² gives simple destabilizing A_n and stabilizing B_n. The right-half-plane modulus bound prevents uncounted crossings from infinity; zero-delay quadratic is Hurwitz. Thus U(tau)=#(A_n<tau)-#(B_n<tau), and B_n<A_{n+1} iff n+1<T, yielding J=max(0,ceil(T)-1), with coincident crossings excluded. The explicit positive parameter family gives T(r)=acos(3/5)*sqrt(1+60/r)/(2pi), J(r)=1,3,11,36 at r=1,.1,.01,.001 and asymptotic sqrt(r)J(r)=sqrt(15)acos(3/5)/pi. These bounded examples corroborate exact analytic reasoning, not an exhaustive scan over delays.
residual_risks: Only the zero-conversion-delay slice and coexistence coefficients 0<alpha<beta, gamma>0.
At critical delays a purely imaginary root excludes exponential stability; nonlinear Hopf criticality and global stable limit cycles are not addressed.
